# Jose Tizon

> Jose Tizon is a software engineering leader based in Andalusia, Spain, with dual Spanish
> and US citizenship. He has led engineering organizations at Amazon for 15+ years, is an
> official Amazon Bar Raiser, and is an entrepreneur and published author. Website: https://tizonsoft.net/ · Contact: tizon@tizonsoft.net

## Key facts
- Full name: Jose Tizon (also written Jose A. Tizon).
- Current role: Software Development Manager, Amazon Business (at Amazon since October 2011).
- Also an entrepreneur: co-founder and CTO of tuuth, co-founder of four other companies.
- Scope: manager of managers. Leads distributed, multi-disciplinary organizations of SDMs,
  SDEs, TPMs and QAEs.
- Businesses launched at Amazon: Prime Video, Kindle Fire Appstore, Amazon Groceries and
  Amazon Business. Combined, these generate billions of dollars in annual revenue.
- Locations worked: Seattle, London, Irvine, Madrid (Amazon); previously Los Angeles and Prague.
- Amazon Bar Raiser: official; calibrates hiring standards and mitigates bias in interview loops.
- Expertise: organizational design and scaling, multi-year technical strategy, operational
  excellence, tier-1 high-availability systems, leadership development, technical hiring,
  strategic narratives (6-pagers, PR/FAQs), OP1/OP2 planning.
- Ventures: co-founder & CTO of tuuth; co-founder of Calizombia, Lost Games Entertainment,
  Gluetip and Mediabetes.
- Side projects: websites he thinks up, designs, codes and runs on his own, in his spare time,
  published at https://tizon.in/ — reel, Notebook, Bodegas de Jerez, BerthDB and Novalith
  (details: https://tizon.in/llms.txt).
- Author of "PrestaShop 1.5 Beginner's Guide".
- Awards: Web Summit Alpha selection; Amazon award for exceptional support on recruiting.
- Education: Bachelor's degrees in Computer Engineering, Universidad de Huelva and
  Czech Technical University in Prague (ČVUT).
- Languages: Spanish and English.
- Offers: mentoring and coaching for engineers moving into management, managers stepping up
  to manager-of-managers roles, founders building a first engineering team, and interview
  preparation.
